facts.claim: RAG was introduced in a 2020 paper by Lewis et al. titled 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks'.
The paper combines a pretrained generator model (parametric memory) with a searchable index of documents (non-parametric memory) accessed by a neural retriever.
An LLM learns from text up to a training cutoff date and does not know later events unless given them.
An LLM can produce hallucinations: fluent answers that are false or unsupported.
In a typical RAG application the LLM's weights are not retrained; retrieved text is added to the prompt at question time.
Knowledge can be updated by adding or replacing documents in the knowledge base, without retraining the LLM.
Documents are split into smaller pieces called chunks before indexing.
An LLM can only process a limited amount of text at once (its context window), so only the most relevant chunks are sent.
An embedding is a list of numbers (a vector) that represents the meaning of a text; texts with similar meaning get similar vectors.
Embeddings are stored in an index or vector database that supports similarity search.
At question time the question is also embedded and the closest chunks (top-k) are retrieved.
The retrieved chunks and the question are combined into one prompt, and the LLM generates the answer from it.
RAG can reduce hallucinations but does not eliminate them.
If retrieval returns irrelevant or wrong chunks, the answer can be wrong.
A RAG system can show which documents it used, so users can check the source.
Common uses: question-answering over company documents, support bots, and 'chat with your PDF' tools.
Fine-tuning changes a model's weights, while RAG supplies information at question time without changing weights.
Chat tools such as ChatGPT are built on LLMs.
An LLM has not seen a person's or company's private documents unless they are given to it.

misconceptions_to_reject: RAG retrains or updates the LLM's weights.
RAG guarantees correct answers / removes all hallucinations.
RAG is the same as a normal search engine.
RAG gives the LLM live access to the whole internet by default.
RAG was invented in 2022 / by a specific company other than the Lewis et al. paper authors.
